scope: Proposition 5.1 (Differences of nearby line sums) of the manuscript “Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising” (preprints/Buffered-comparison-and-stopping-band-resolution-in-critical-Ising-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d5167e3fe5fb85f4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 19-20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Js, J′ s be two parallel horizontal or vertical lattice segments of lengths O(s) whose matching portions differ by a displacement of length at most Cw and whose unmatched end pieces have total length O(w). The same statement is allowed for two concentric square contours of radii comparable to s and radius difference at most Cw, by matching their four sides. Assume the union has a free neighborhood of width cs and is covered by a fixed number of buffered planar charts. Set MJs = s−7/8 X Js σx, MJ′ s = s−7/8 X J′ s σx. 19 There is a constant C0, depending only on the fixed geometry and the buffer, such that, for each fixed h = w/s ∈ (0, h0], lim sup s→∞ ∥MJs − MJ′ s ∥2 ≤ C0h3/8 . (5.1) The law may have arbitrary common pins beyond the buffer or be a mixture of such laws. The same conclusion holds for nearby full periodic rows of period W, normalized by s−7/8, when W/s is fixed and positive; its constant may depend on this ratio.
